newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian government says new U.S. envoy named.
newsitem.headline: Colombian government says new U.S. envoy named.

text.p: Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia said Friday that the United States had appointed a new U.S. ambassador to Colombia, Curtis Kamman.
In interviews with Colombian radio, Mejia said that Kamman, currently U.S. ambassador to Bolivia, had been named to replace outgoing ambassador Myles Frechette.
"We've already given the Colombian government's consent to the naming of the new ambassador," Mejia said, adding that this had been requested by Washington on May 22.
There was no immediate announcement in Washington of appointment of a new ambassador, and the U.S. embassy here declined to confirm Kamman's appointment.
But it issued a statement denying local media reports that Frechette had resigned.
"The ambassador has said repeatedly that he plans to leave the country between July and December," the embassy said, alluding to the usual three-year timetable for ambassadorial postings.
"Once President Clinton has designated his replacement, that person must be approved by the United States Senate. That process normally takes some months," it said.
Frechette took over as envoy to Bogota in June 1994, shortly before a political crisis erupted over charges that Colombian President Ernesto Samper financed his election with drug money.
As ambassador, he saw U.S.-Colombia ties plunge to a new low because of the scandal and what U.S. officials describe as high- level corruption in Samper's administration.
